Subject: Rolling renewal anchoring & usage hedge proposal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the constructive discussion last week. I promised to send a concrete option that balances Acme's predictable spend needs with flexibility for seasonal/AI-demo driven spikes. Attached is a short proposal (PDF) but the core idea is below:

- Term: 36 months with an "anchor month" (month 1 of the term) that sets the baseline monthly credit for billing; subsequent months roll to average usage unless you elect a monthly top-up.
- Ramp schedule: Year 1 is staged (60% baseline / 30% reserved burst / 10% on-demand), Year 2 moves to 75% baseline, Year 3 to 85% baseline.
- Auto-align clause: if average trailing-3-month usage exceeds 125% of baseline for two consecutive quarters, we auto-adjust baseline upward with pre-agreed price ladder to avoid mid-term invoices and re-consent headaches.
- Upsell/top-up: one-click capacity top-ups (charged pro rata) and an annual true-up credit if you under-consume.

Why this helps Acme: predictable committed cost for forecasting, burst safety during product launches, and a simple path to increase baseline without re-contracting.

Next steps I suggest: 1) procurement review on their cadence, 2) Kimberly to confirm invoice cadence and any proration rules, 3) Marissa to outline onboarding ramp and success milestones tied to capacity increases.

Attachment: 20261130-anchored-3yr-proposal.pdf (pdf)

If that looks reasonable I can send a clean DocuSign for signature and a separate invoice cadence options sheet.

Best,
Sergio
